context: The Web UI currently has a navigation menu (navbar) at the top with tabs like 'Active Prompt', 'Prompts History', 'Workdir', 'Files', and 'Help'. Currently, when users scroll down the page content, the menu scrolls out of view. The requirement is to make this menu stay visible while scrolling. This questionnaire helps decide the best implementation approach for keeping the menu accessible at all times.

questions.question-text: Which CSS positioning strategy should be used to keep the navbar visible while scrolling?

options.label: Use CSS 'position: fixed' to fix the navbar at the top of the viewport
options.pros: Simple implementation, navbar always visible at the same position, works in all modern browsers, no JavaScript required, predictable behavior
options.cons: Fixed elements are removed from normal document flow and may require adjusting content padding to prevent overlap, navbar won't scroll with page header if present

options.label: Use CSS 'position: sticky' to make the navbar stick when scrolling reaches it
options.pros: Modern CSS solution, navbar scrolls naturally until it reaches top then sticks, remains in document flow until sticky, elegant user experience, no content overlap issues initially
options.cons: Slightly less browser support (though still good in modern browsers), requires understanding of sticky positioning context, may have quirks with parent containers

options.label: Use JavaScript scroll detection to toggle fixed positioning dynamically
options.pros: Full control over behavior, can add smooth transitions and animations, can handle complex logic like hiding/showing on scroll direction
options.cons: More complex implementation, requires JavaScript execution, potential performance issues if not optimized, more code to maintain, unnecessary complexity for simple sticky behavior

questions.recommendation-rationale: Using 'position: fixed' is recommended because it's the most straightforward and reliable solution. The navbar is currently at the top of the page, so making it fixed ensures it's always visible without any complexity. The minimal adjustment needed is adding top padding to the main content to prevent the fixed navbar from overlapping content. This is standard practice for sticky headers and provides consistent behavior across all browsers.

questions.question-text: Should the navbar have any visual changes when it becomes fixed (shadow, transparency, etc.)?

options.label: Add a bottom shadow to create depth and separation from content
options.pros: Provides visual cue that navbar is floating above content, improves UI depth perception, standard design pattern for fixed headers, helps with readability
options.cons: Adds visual complexity, may not match current design aesthetic if it's minimalist

options.label: Keep the navbar appearance exactly as is without any visual changes
options.pros: Maintains consistent design, simpler implementation, no risk of visual conflicts, cleaner look
options.cons: May lack visual indication that it's a fixed element, less depth in the interface

options.label: Add both shadow and slightly adjust the background opacity/color
options.pros: Strong visual distinction, modern look, clear indication of fixed state, professional appearance
options.cons: More complex CSS, may feel too heavy or distracting, requires careful color selection to maintain readability

questions.recommendation-rationale: Adding a bottom shadow is recommended as it's a common UI pattern that provides subtle visual feedback without being intrusive. It helps users understand that the navbar is a fixed element floating above the content, improving the overall user experience. The shadow is professional, widely accepted, and easy to implement with a simple CSS box-shadow property.

questions.question-text: How should the main content area padding be adjusted to accommodate the fixed navbar?

options.label: Add exact pixel padding matching the navbar height to the container-fluid
options.pros: Precise control, prevents any content from being hidden under navbar, works reliably
options.cons: Hardcoded pixel values may need updating if navbar height changes, less flexible for responsive design

options.label: Use CSS calc() or variable to dynamically adjust padding based on navbar height
options.pros: More maintainable, adapts automatically if navbar height changes, modern CSS approach, flexible
options.cons: Slightly more complex CSS, need to ensure navbar height is accessible as a CSS variable

options.label: Add generous padding (e.g., 80-100px) to ensure content is never hidden
options.pros: Simple approach, definitely prevents overlap, no precise measurement needed
options.cons: May create too much empty space, looks awkward if navbar is smaller than the padding, wastes vertical space

questions.recommendation-rationale: Using exact pixel padding is recommended for simplicity and reliability. The Bootstrap navbar has a predictable height (typically around 56-60px), and adding a matching padding value ensures content is never hidden. While CSS variables would be more elegant, the navbar height is unlikely to change frequently, making the simple approach more practical. This can be easily adjusted in the future if needed.
